newsitem.title: INDIA: India Castrol sees 1997 second half as difficult.
newsitem.headline: India Castrol sees 1997 second half as difficult.

text.p: Indian lubricant maker Castrol India Ltd. said on Tuesday it expected a difficult second half in 1997.

"The trading conditions in the second half of the year are expected to be tough, with the deterioration in industrial growth, especially in the heavy engineering industry and automobile sector, where a considerable slowdown in evident," the firm said in a statement shortly after it announced glowing first half results.
"This will put pressure on margins," it cautioned.

Castrol, which is the Indian arm of British firm Burmah- Castrol Plc.,, said its first-half sales had risen by 654.9 million rupees to 4.89 billion rupees, as compared to 4.23 billion in the corresponding period the previous year.

"The company has done well in the consumer business with icnreased margins because of trading up and the success of new product initiatives launched during the course of last year," the statement said.
"In addition to improving margins, the company has also been able to grow its volumes both in the consumer sector and the industrial sector."
The statement said volumes had grown at 12 percent, showing what it called Castrol's ability to expand market share and retain consumer loyalty against tough and intense competition.
Burmah Castrol Plc has a 51 percent equity stake in Castrol India.
